tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 1
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A student guesses independently on a $10$-question true/false quiz, so each answer is correct with probability $0.5$. The probability of getting exactly $7$ correct is strictly less than $0.12$.
A call centre handles $8$ independent calls, each closing with probability $0.3$. The manager claims that the chance of at least one closed call is below $90\%$.
A factory inspects $20$ independent parts, each defective with probability $0.1$. The expected number of defects is greater than the standard deviation of the defect count.
Two players each take $12$ independent shots; one scores with probability $0.4$ and the other with probability $0.6$. The first player's score count has strictly larger variance.
A safety panel contains $4$ independent switches, each working with probability $1/2$. The probability that at least one switch works is exactly $15/16$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=7)&=\binom{10}{7}(0.5)^{10}=\frac{120}{1024} \\ &\approx0.11719<0.12
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge1)&=1-P(X=0)=1-(0.7)^8 \\ &\approx0.94235>0.90
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=20(0.1)=2 \\ \operatorname{SD}(X)&=\sqrt{20(0.1)(0.9)}=\sqrt{1.8}\approx1.342<2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}(X)&=12(0.4)(0.6)=2.88 \\ \operatorname{Var}(Y)&=12(0.6)(0.4)=2.88
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Exact probabilities, complements, moments, and variance comparisons in binomial settings.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 2
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A greenhouse plants $6$ independent seeds, each germinating with probability $1/3$. A researcher claims that the probability of exactly $2$ germinations is below $0.30$.
A salesperson gives $5$ independent demonstrations, each succeeding with probability $0.4$. The probability of at least $4$ successes is greater than $0.08$.
A student guesses on $12$ independent true/false questions. The instructor claims that the number correct has equal mean and variance.
Student A answers $10$ questions correctly with probability $0.3$ each, while student B does so with probability $0.7$ each. A's correct count has the same distribution as B's incorrect count.
A campaign compares $5$ and $10$ independent contacts, each converting with probability $0.2$. Doubling the contacts from $5$ to $10$ exactly doubles the chance of at least one conversion.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=2)&=\binom62\left(\frac13\right)^2\left(\frac23\right)^4 \\ &=\frac{80}{243}\approx0.32922>0.30
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge4)&=\binom54(0.4)^4(0.6)+(0.4)^5 \\ &=0.0768+0.01024=0.08704>0.08
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=12(0.5)=6 \\ \operatorname{Var}(X)&=12(0.5)(0.5)=3\ne6
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
X&\sim\operatorname{Bin}(10,0.3) \\ 10-Y&\sim\operatorname{Bin}(10,1-0.7)=\operatorname{Bin}(10,0.3)
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_5&=1-(0.8)^5\approx0.67232 \\ P_{10}&=1-(0.8)^{10}\approx0.89263\ne2P_5
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Binomial mass, upper tails, moments, complementary success rates, and nonlinear complements.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 3
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A basketball player takes $4$ independent shots with success probability $0.5$. The combined probability of making either none of the shots or all four shots is exactly $1/8$.
A lab tests $8$ independent samples, each positive with probability $0.25$. It reports that $P(X\le1)$ is strictly less than $(0.75)^8+8(0.25)(0.75)^7$.
A goalkeeper faces $9$ independent penalties and saves each with probability $1/3$. The save count has mean $3$ and variance $2$.
Two factories each inspect $100$ items; defect probabilities are $0.1$ and $0.5$. The first factory's defect count has larger variance than the second's.
A backup system runs $n$ independent units, each activating with probability $p$. Its probability of at least one activation is $1-(1-p)^n$, whereas $np$ is only the expected count.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=0\ \text{or}\ X=4)&=(0.5)^4+(0.5)^4 \\ &=\frac1{16}+\frac1{16}=\frac18
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\le1)&=P(X=0)+P(X=1) \\ &=(0.75)^8+8(0.25)(0.75)^7
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=9\left(\frac13\right)=3 \\ \operatorname{Var}(X)&=9\left(\frac13\right)\left(\frac23\right)=2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}(X)&=100(0.1)(0.9)=9 \\ \operatorname{Var}(Y)&=100(0.5)(0.5)=25>9
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge1)&=1-P(X=0)=1-(1-p)^n \\ E(X)&=np
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Symmetric outcomes, lower tails, binomial moments, variance size, and at-least-one events.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 4
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A fair coin is tossed $7$ times. A student claims that the combined probability of exactly $3$ or exactly $4$ heads is $35/128$.
A student guesses on $6$ independent true/false items. By symmetry, the chance of at least $4$ correct answers equals the chance of at most $2$ correct answers.
A lab keeps $n=10$ trials but raises success probability from $0.2$ to $0.4$. An analyst claims that this change exactly doubles the binomial variance.
One server delivers each of $5$ messages with probability $0.2$, while another does so with probability $0.8$. The chance of exactly $1$ delivery on the first equals exactly $4$ on the second.
A machine makes $3$ independent attempts, each succeeding with probability $0.1$. A supervisor claims that the chance of at least one success is exactly $0.30$.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge4)&=P(X=4)+P(X=5)+P(X=6) \\ &=P(X=2)+P(X=1)+P(X=0)=P(X\le2)
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_{0.2}&=10(0.2)(0.8)=1.6 \\ V_{0.4}&=10(0.4)(0.6)=2.4\ne2(1.6)
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=1)&=\binom51(0.2)(0.8)^4 \\ P(Y=4)&=\binom54(0.8)^4(0.2)=P(X=1)
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge1)&=1-(0.9)^3 \\ &=1-0.729=0.271\ne0.30
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Fair-trial symmetry, variance changes, complementary binomial counts, and complements.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 5
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A pitcher throws $3$ independent strikes, each with probability $0.4$. The probability of throwing exactly one strike is exactly $54/125$.
A student guesses on $10$ independent true/false questions. The probability of getting at least $6$ answers correct is greater than $1/2$.
A bottling line checks $20$ independent bottles, each underfilled with probability $0.25$. The count has mean $5$ and standard deviation $\sqrt{3.75}$.
A quality analyst counts defects in $n$ independent items with defect chance $p$. She claims the ratio $P(X=k+1)/P(X=k)$ equals $\frac{k+1}{n-k}\frac{p}{1-p}$.
A fair-component test changes from $4$ to $5$ independent components. The chance that none pass is multiplied by exactly $1/2$.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge6)&=\frac{1-P(X=5)}2 \\ &=\frac{1-\binom{10}{5}/2^{10}}2\approx0.37695<\frac12
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_4(X=0)&=\left(\frac12\right)^4 \\ \frac{P_5(X=0)}{P_4(X=0)}&=\frac{(1/2)^5}{(1/2)^4}=\frac12
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Exact mass, majority tails, moments, consecutive probabilities, and zero-success scaling.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 6
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A player takes $5$ independent penalties and scores each with probability $0.6$. A commentator claims the chance of scoring all five exceeds $0.08$.
A sales team makes $4$ independent calls, each closing with probability $0.3$. The chance of at least one close is exactly $1-(0.7)^4$.
A factory checks $16$ independent parts, each defective with probability $0.25$. A report claims that the defect count's variance equals its mean.
Two quizzes each have $8$ independent items, with success probabilities $0.5$ and $0.25$. The first expected score is exactly twice the second expected score.
A fair die is rolled $4$ times independently. A student claims that the probability of seeing at least one six exceeds $0.55$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=5)&=(0.6)^5=0.07776 \\ 0.07776&<0.08
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge1)&=1-P(X=0) \\ &=1-(1-0.3)^4=1-(0.7)^4
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=16(0.25)=4 \\ \operatorname{Var}(X)&=16(0.25)(0.75)=3\ne4
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=8(0.5)=4,\quad E(Y)=8(0.25)=2 \\ \frac{E(X)}{E(Y)}&=2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge1)&=1-\left(\frac56\right)^4 \\ &=\frac{671}{1296}\approx0.51775<0.55
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: All-success events, at-least-one events, moments, ratios of means, and die trials.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 7
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A fair coin is tossed $9$ times. The probability of obtaining exactly $5$ heads is exactly $63/256$.
A marketer sends $7$ independent offers, each accepted with probability $0.2$. She computes the chance of at least $2$ acceptances as $1-P(X=0)$.
A rare-fault test examines $50$ independent devices, each failing with probability $0.02$. The failure count has mean $1$ and variance strictly below $1$.
Two archers take $12$ independent shots with hit probabilities $0.4$ and $0.6$. A coach claims that the second archer's hit count has larger standard deviation.
A monitoring system has fixed alert probability $p$ with $0<p<1$ on each independent check. The probability of at least one alert strictly increases as the positive number of checks increases.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge2)&=1-P(X=0)-P(X=1) \\ &\ne1-P(X=0)
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=50(0.02)=1 \\ \operatorname{Var}(X)&=50(0.02)(0.98)=0.98<1
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}(X)&=12(0.4)(0.6)=2.88 \\ \operatorname{Var}(Y)&=12(0.6)(0.4)=2.88
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_n(X\ge1)&=1-(1-p)^n \\ P_{n+1}-P_n&=p(1-p)^n>0
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Fair-trial mass, tail complements, rare-event moments, symmetric variances, and monotonicity.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 8
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A lab runs $4$ independent assays, each positive with probability $0.25$. A scientist claims that the chance of exactly $2$ positives exceeds $0.22$.
A student guesses independently on $5$ true/false questions. The chance of at least $3$ correct equals the chance of at most $2$ correct.
A premium machine passes each of $10$ independent tests with probability $0.9$. A manager claims the standard deviation of its pass count is exactly $0.9$.
One fair-coin experiment uses $5$ tosses and another uses $10$. The second experiment has exactly twice both the expected head count and its variance.
A server makes $6$ independent attempts with success probability $1/3$. A technician claims that the chance of no successes exceeds $0.10$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=2)&=\binom42(0.25)^2(0.75)^2 \\ &=\frac{27}{128}\approx0.21094<0.22
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge3)&=P(X=3)+P(X=4)+P(X=5) \\ &=P(X=2)+P(X=1)+P(X=0)=P(X\le2)
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}(X)&=10(0.9)(0.1)=0.9 \\ \operatorname{SD}(X)&=\sqrt{0.9}\ne0.9
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_5&=2.5,\quad E_{10}=5=2E_5 \\ V_5&=1.25,\quad V_{10}=2.5=2V_5
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=0)&=\left(\frac23\right)^6=\frac{64}{729} \\ &\approx0.08779<0.10
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Exact probability checks, fair symmetry, standard deviation, scaling in trial count, and no-success events.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 9
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A student guesses on $8$ independent true/false questions. The probability of getting exactly $4$ correct is exactly $35/128$.
A player takes $3$ independent shots with scoring probability $0.8$. A reporter says the probability of at least $2$ scores is just $3(0.8)^2(0.2)$.
A plant inspects $25$ independent items, each defective with probability $0.2$. The defect count's variance is $4$, which is below its mean of $5$.
A clerk records one six-toss fair-coin head count as $X$ and copies the same count as $Y=X$. The clerk claims that $X+Y$ has a $\operatorname{Bin}(12,0.5)$ distribution.
A salesperson makes $2$ independent attempts with success probability $0.4$. The chance of at least one success is $0.64$, which is less than the expected count $0.8$.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge2)&=P(X=2)+P(X=3) \\ &=3(0.8)^2(0.2)+(0.8)^3
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=25(0.2)=5 \\ \operatorname{Var}(X)&=25(0.2)(0.8)=4<5
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
X+Y&=2X\in\{0,2,4,\ldots,12\} \\ P(X+Y=1)&=0,\quad P(\operatorname{Bin}(12,0.5)=1)>0
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge1)&=1-(0.6)^2=0.64 \\ E(X)&=2(0.4)=0.8>0.64
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Central probability, upper tails, moments, dependence, and an at-least-one bound.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 10
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A campaign sends $5$ independent messages, each answered with probability $0.2$. An analyst claims that the probability of no answers is below $0.30$.
A fair coin is tossed $9$ times. The probability of at most $3$ heads equals the probability of at least $6$ heads.
A survey asks $18$ independent respondents a question with yes probability $1/3$. A report says the yes count has mean $6$ and standard deviation $4$.
A designer can choose a success probability $p$ for a fixed number $n$ of independent trials. The binomial variance is largest at $p=1/2$.
A building has $10$ independent alarms, each triggering with probability $0.05$. A technician claims that the chance of at least one trigger exceeds $0.50$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=0)&=(0.8)^5=0.32768 \\ 0.32768&>0.30
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\le3)&=P(X=0)+\cdots+P(X=3) \\ &=P(X=9)+\cdots+P(X=6)=P(X\ge6)
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=18\left(\frac13\right)=6 \\ \operatorname{SD}(X)&=\sqrt{18(1/3)(2/3)}=2\ne4
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}(X)&=np(1-p)=n\left(\frac14-\left(p-\frac12\right)^2\right) \\ \max\operatorname{Var}(X)&=\frac n4\ \text{at }p=\frac12
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge1)&=1-(0.95)^{10} \\ &\approx0.40126<0.50
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: No-success probability, symmetric tails, moments, maximum variance, and alarms.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 11
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A fair coin is tossed $6$ times. The probability of exactly $3$ heads is below $1/3$.
A machine runs $4$ independent tests with pass probability $0.25$. An engineer calculates $P(X\ge3)$ as only $\binom43(0.25)^3(0.75)$.
A network checks $30$ independent links, each failing with probability $0.1$. The failure count has expected value $3$ and variance $2.7$.
Two teams each attempt $7$ independent tasks, with success probabilities $0.4$ and $0.6$. A manager claims their expected total number of successes is $14$.
A student guesses on $3$ independent true/false questions. The probability of at least one correct answer is exactly $7/8$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=3)&=\binom63\left(\frac12\right)^6=\frac{20}{64} \\ &=\frac5{16}=0.3125<\frac13
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge3)&=P(X=3)+P(X=4) \\ &=\binom43(0.25)^3(0.75)+(0.25)^4
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=30(0.1)=3 \\ \operatorname{Var}(X)&=30(0.1)(0.9)=2.7
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X+Y)&=7(0.4)+7(0.6) \\ &=2.8+4.2=7\ne14
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge1)&=1-P(X=0) \\ &=1-\left(\frac12\right)^3=\frac78
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Central mass, upper tails, rare-event moments, expected totals, and fair complements.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 12
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A call centre receives $10$ independent sales opportunities, each closing with probability $0.2$. A supervisor claims the probability of exactly $2$ closes is exactly $0.32$.
A student guesses independently on $5$ true/false questions. The probability of at least one correct answer is exactly $31/32$.
A clinic observes $12$ independent treatments, each effective with probability $0.25$. A report states that the standard deviation of the effective-treatment count is $2.25$.
A binomial count records successes in $n$ independent trials with success probability $p\in(0,1)$. Its variance-to-mean ratio is exactly $1-p$.
A five-contact campaign raises each contact's conversion probability from $0.1$ to $0.2$. A manager claims this change more than doubles the chance of at least one conversion.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=2)&=\binom{10}{2}(0.2)^2(0.8)^8 \\ &\approx0.30199\ne0.32
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}(X)&=12(0.25)(0.75)=2.25 \\ \operatorname{SD}(X)&=\sqrt{2.25}=1.5\ne2.25
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{E(X)}&=\frac{np(1-p)}{np} \\ &=1-p
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Point probability, fair complements, standard deviation, dispersion ratio, and probability changes.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 13
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A student guesses on $7$ independent true/false items. The probability of getting no answers correct is exactly $1/128$.
A salesperson makes $6$ independent calls with close probability $0.4$. A report computes the probability of more than $5$ closes by adding both the $5$-close and $6$-close probabilities.
A fair coin is tossed $40$ times independently. The head count has mean $20$ and variance $10$.
A lab counts positives in $9$ trials as $X$, then sets $Y=X$ rather than running new trials. It claims that $X+Y$ is binomial with $18$ trials and the same success probability $0.3$.

A student records the number of successes in a fixed set of trials and also the waiting time to the first success. Even with the same $p$, the first variable is binomial and the second is geometric, not binomial.
tactical_explanations:
**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=40(0.5)=20 \\ \operatorname{Var}(X)&=40(0.5)(0.5)=10
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Zero-success events, singleton tails, moments, dependent sums, and distribution choice.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 14
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A candidate answers $5$ independent multiple-choice questions correctly with probability $0.4$ each. A tutor claims that the chance of exactly $3$ correct answers is $0.24$.
A fair coin is tossed $8$ times. The probability of at most $2$ heads equals the probability of at least $6$ heads.
A factory checks $15$ independent items, each defective with probability $0.2$. An inspector claims the defect count's standard deviation exceeds its mean.
Two production lines each inspect $20$ independent parts, with defect probabilities $0.3$ and $0.1$. The first line's defect-count variance is larger.
A sample contains $20$ independent items, each defective with probability $0.01$. A manager claims that the chance of at least one defective item exceeds $0.20$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=3)&=\binom53(0.4)^3(0.6)^2 \\ &=10(0.064)(0.36)=0.2304\ne0.24
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=k)&=P(X=8-k) \\ P(X\le2)&=P(X\ge6)
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=15(0.2)=3 \\ \operatorname{SD}(X)&=\sqrt{15(0.2)(0.8)}=\sqrt{2.4}\approx1.549<3
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_{0.3}&=20(0.3)(0.7)=4.2 \\ V_{0.1}&=20(0.1)(0.9)=1.8<4.2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge1)&=1-(0.99)^{20} \\ &\approx0.18209<0.20
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Decimal probability, symmetric tails, mean versus standard deviation, variance comparison, and rare events.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 15
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A student guesses on $3$ independent true/false items. For scores $0,1,2,3$, the probability distribution is exactly $(1/8,3/8,3/8,1/8)$.
A sales team makes $10$ independent calls, each closing with probability $0.4$. It claims that the chance of at least $9$ closes is just $(0.4)^{10}$.
A fair die is rolled $24$ times and sixes are counted. The count has expected value $4$ and variance $10/3$, which is below the mean.
A quality team records $X$ successes in $n$ trials and then counts failures as $n-X$. It claims the failure count's variance is $n^{2}$ times the success count's variance.
A reliability analyst expands the chance of at least one success in $n$ independent trials. The sum $\sum_{k=1}^{n}\binom nkp^k(1-p)^{n-k}$ equals $1-(1-p)^n$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=k)&=\binom3k\left(\frac12\right)^3 \\ (P_0,P_1,P_2,P_3)&=\frac18(1,3,3,1)
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=24\left(\frac16\right)=4 \\ \operatorname{Var}(X)&=24\left(\frac16\right)\left(\frac56\right)=\frac{10}{3}<4
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}(n-X)&=(-1)^2\operatorname{Var}(X) \\ &=\operatorname{Var}(X),\ \text{not }n^2\operatorname{Var}(X)
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom nkp^k(1-p)^{n-k}&=1 \\ \sum_{k=1}^{n}\binom nkp^k(1-p)^{n-k}&=1-(1-p)^n
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Full distributions, extreme tails, moments, transformed variance, and binomial expansion.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 16
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A machine passes each of $4$ independent tests with probability $0.6$. A technician claims the chance of exactly $2$ passes is $0.36$.
A student guesses on $12$ independent true/false questions. The probability of at least $7$ correct answers equals the probability of at most $5$ correct answers.
A fair coin is tossed $9$ times. A report claims that the head count's mean equals its variance.
Two inspection plans use $20$ and $40$ independent items with the same defect probability $0.25$. Doubling the item count doubles both the mean and variance of the defect count.
A campaign makes $8$ independent contacts with conversion probability $0.25$. A manager claims the chance of at least one conversion exceeds $0.90$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=2)&=\binom42(0.6)^2(0.4)^2 \\ &=6(0.36)(0.16)=0.3456\ne0.36
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=6+j)&=P(X=6-j) \\ P(X\ge7)&=P(X\le5)
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(X)&=9(0.5)=4.5 \\ \operatorname{Var}(X)&=9(0.5)(0.5)=2.25\ne4.5
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{E(Y)}{E(X)}&=\frac{40(0.25)}{20(0.25)}=2 \\ \frac{\operatorname{Var}(Y)}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}&=\frac{40(0.25)(0.75)}{20(0.25)(0.75)}=2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge1)&=1-(0.75)^8 \\ &\approx0.89989<0.90
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Probability mass, symmetric tails, fair-trial moments, scaling with trial count, and a tight bound.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 17
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A student guesses on $11$ independent true/false questions. The probabilities of exactly $5$ and exactly $6$ correct are equal, and each is $\binom{11}{5}/2^{11}$.
A call centre handles $6$ independent calls, each closing with probability $0.3$. A supervisor claims that the chance of at most one close is simply $(0.7)^6$.
A fair coin is tossed $14$ times. The variance of the number of heads is exactly $3.5$.
A student claims that the number of heads in $10$ fixed tosses and the number of tosses until the first head have the same distribution because both use $p=0.5$.
A monitoring system performs $n>0$ independent checks. Replacing alert probability $p=0.2$ by $0.8$ changes the probability of at least one alert.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\le1)&=P(X=0)+P(X=1) \\ &=(0.7)^6+6(0.3)(0.7)^5>(0.7)^6
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}(X)&=14(0.5)(0.5)=3.5
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_{0.2}(X\ge1)&=1-(0.8)^n \\ P_{0.8}(X\ge1)&=1-(0.2)^n,\quad n>0
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Twin central probabilities, lower tails, fair variance, distribution confusion, and complementary probabilities.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 18
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A server makes $2$ independent connection attempts, each succeeding with probability $0.3$. An engineer claims that the probability of exactly one success is $0.49$.
A fair coin is tossed $15$ times. The probability of at least $8$ heads equals the probability of at most $7$ heads, so each event has probability $1/2$.
A player takes $8$ independent shots with scoring probability $0.75$. A coach claims the standard deviation of the score count is exactly $1.5$.
Two independent test plans use $5$ and $20$ items, each failing with probability $0.2$. The ratio of their no-failure probabilities, $P_{20}(0)/P_{5}(0)$, is $(0.8)^{15}$.
A campaign runs $n$ independent trials with success probability $p\in(0,1)$. A planner claims that $1-(1-p)^n$ is the probability of at least two successes.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=1)&=\binom21(0.3)(0.7) \\ &=0.42\ne0.49
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=k)&=P(X=15-k) \\ P(X\ge8)&=P(X\le7)=\frac12
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}(X)&=8(0.75)(0.25)=1.5 \\ \operatorname{SD}(X)&=\sqrt{1.5}\ne1.5
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 19
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A sensor runs $8$ independent checks, each alerting with probability $1/3$. The probability of receiving no alerts is less than $0.04$.
A student guesses on $4$ independent true/false questions. A tutor claims that the probability of at least $2$ correct answers is exactly $3/4$.
A manufacturer checks $100$ independent products, each defective with probability $0.05$. The defect count has mean $5$ and standard deviation $\sqrt{4.75}$.
Two binomial inspection plans have the same expected number of defects $np$. A manager claims this equality forces the two defect counts to have the same variance.
A machine performs one trial with success probability $p$. In this one-trial case, the probability of at least one success is exactly $p$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X=0)&=\left(\frac23\right)^8=\frac{256}{6561} \\ &\approx0.03902<0.04
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X\ge2)&=1-P(X=0)-P(X=1) \\ &=1-\frac1{16}-\frac4{16}=\frac{11}{16}\ne\frac34
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}

\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

$$
\begin{aligned}
